reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, batch 1

samples_reviewed.question_text: Measure the object. Its length is ___ paperclips.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ paperclips.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ paperclips.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency requires comparing two measured lengths/distances, but the comparing_ordering samples strip out any unit context ('Which is greater: 10 or 6?') and the length_measurement samples only measure a single object ('Its length is ___ paperclips.'); no sampled item asks the student to compare two measured lengths against each other.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: length_measurement (2 axes/4 combos) plus comparing_ordering (3 axes/8 combos) register 12 combos total per variant_registry, checked exhaustively by validate_matrix; the 5 seeds here are illustrative only.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: All observed prompts are short, single-clause, and under the 15-word grade-1 cap, appropriate reading demand for this grade/quarter.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The comparing_ordering variant as sampled produces bare-integer comparisons unconnected to any measured unit, so the registered 8-combo space does not visibly demonstrate coverage of the actual 'compare two measured lengths' skill this node names.

competency_alignment.rationale: Comparing raw integers (10 vs 6) is a numeracy skill from a different competency strand, not the measurement-comparison skill, e.g. 'this pencil is longer, measured in paperclips', that this specific node's wording requires.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The magnitudes involved (5-30) are all small and grade-1-appropriate regardless of the framing mismatch, so scale is not the driver of the concern.
